==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:actyf|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}}
From {{inh|en|enm|actyf}}, from {{der|en|fro|actif}}, from {{der|en|la|activus|alt=āctīv(us)}}, from {{m|la|ago|agere|t=to do, to act}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂éǵeti}}. {{surf|+suf|en|act|ive}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈæk.tɪv/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-active.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|æktɪv|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|ac|tive}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Having the power or quality of acting; causing change; communicating action or motion; acting;—opposed to [[passive]], that receives.
#: {{syn|en|acting}}
#: {{ant|en|passive}}
#: {{co|en|certain '''active''' principles}}
#: {{co|en|the '''active''' powers of the mind}}
# Quick in physical movement; of an agile and vigorous body; nimble.
#: {{syn|en|agile|nimble}}
#: {{ant|en|passive|indolent|still}}
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' child or animal}}
# In action; actually proceeding; working; in force
#: {{syn|en|in action|working|in force}}
#: {{ant|en|quiescent|dormant|extinct}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' laws}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' hostilities}}
## {{lb|en|specifically|of certain geological features, such as volcano, geysers, etc}} Emitting hot materials, such as lava, smoke, or steam, or producing [[tremor]]s.
# Given to action; constantly engaged in action; energetic; diligent; busy
#: {{syn|en|busy|deedful|diligent|energetic}}
#: {{ant|en|dull|sluggish|indolent|inert}}
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' man of business}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' mind}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' zeal}}
#* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text=This new-comer was a man who in any company would have seemed striking.{{...}}He was smooth-faced, and his fresh skin and well-developed figure bespoke the man in good physical condition through '''active''' exercise, yet well content with the world's apportionment.}}
# Requiring or implying action or exertion
#: {{syn|en|operative}}
#: {{ant|en|passive|tranquil|sedentary}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' employment or service}}
#: {{co|en|'''active''' scenes}}
# Given to action rather than contemplation; practical; operative
#: {{ant|en|theoretical|speculative}}
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' rather than a speculative statesman}}
# Brisk; lively.
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' demand for corn}}
# Implying or producing rapid action.
#: {{ant|en|passive|slow}}
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' disease}}
#: {{co|en|an '''active''' remedy}}
# {{senseid|en|grammar}} {{lb|en|heading|grammar}} ''About verbs.''
## Applied to a form of the verb; — opposed to [[passive]]. See [[active voice]].
## Applied to verbs which assert that the subject acts upon or affects something else; transitive.
## Applied to all verbs that express action as distinct from mere existence or state.
# {{lb|en|computing|of [[source code]]}} Eligible to be processed by a [[compiler]] or [[interpreter]].
#* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=2006-12-24|author=David Williams|title=satellite program
|url=https://groups.google.com/forum/#!original/comp.lang.basic.visual.misc/WnnQLluT4Is/qTIAdKigS9cJ|newsgroup=comp.lang.basic.visual.misc|passage=I think it should be upgraded to Visual BASIC, but I'm no good at that. So maybe someone here would like to take a crack at it. There are only 40 lines of '''active''' code, plus a few REMs. About 100 BASIC commands altogether.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Chris Grover|title=Adobe Edge Preview 5: The Missing Manual|chapter=Triggering Actions|edition=3rd|location=Sebastopol|publisher=O'Reilly Media|isbn=9781449330309|page={{gbooks|ayjDz3cj_ogC|98|active}}|passage=Edge uses green text for comments. This makes it easier for you to quickly differentiate between '''active''' code and comments.}}
# {{lb|en|electronics}} Not [[passive]].
# {{lb|en|gay slang|of a homosexual man}} enjoying a role in [[anal sex]] in which he [[penetrate]]s, rather than being penetrated by his partner.
#: {{syn|en|top}}
#: {{ant|en|passive|bottom}}

====Synonyms====
* See also [[Thesaurus:active]]

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A person or thing that is acting or [[capable]] of acting.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1989|journal=The Alcalde|volume=78|issue=2|page=11
|passage="Alumni could become more active in giving guidance and leadership to students. They act as sort of a 'maturity governor' on fraternities," notes Ratliff, citing surveys suggesting that fraternity '''actives''' presume mistakenly that alumni want hazing {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|electronics}} Any component that is not [[passive]]. See {{w|Passivity (engineering)}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=David Manners|title=Hitchhikers' Guide to Electronics in the '90s|page=36
|passage=Components are split into two broad segments: '''actives''' and passives. Active components like the vacuum tube and the transistor contain the power to generate and alter electrical signals.}}
